lucky-bamboo: Lucky bamboo isn't bamboo at all — it's a Dracaena that grows happily in just water and pebbles.
aglaonema-snow-white: Aglaonema is one of the most forgiving houseplants — it tolerates low light, dry air and irregular watering.
dracena-fragrans: 'Fragrans' refers to its rare flowers — old plants occasionally burst into fragrant white blooms overnight.
rainbow-cactus: The rainbow cactus's colours come from careful sun exposure — growers gradually 'sun-stress' it to paint the top.
echivera-succullent: Echeveria rosettes always face the sun — turn the pot and the plant will slowly re-orient itself over days.
wandering-jew-with-pot: Tradescantia grows so fast it can double its trailing length in weeks — one of the fastest houseplants there is.
passiflora-incarnata-rakhi-bel: The passion flower's intricate bloom looks man-made — it once inspired a legend about the crown of thorns.
trumpet-vine-orange: Trumpet vine's flowers are shaped like horns to funnel pollinators deep inside — hummingbirds queue up for them in the Americas.
money-tree-pachira-aquatica: The money tree survives flooding — in the wild it grows along riverbanks with its roots underwater for weeks.
rubber-plant-2: The rubber plant's milky sap was once a real rubber source — Ficus elastica literally built early rubber goods.
singonium: Syngonium leaves change shape as the plant matures — arrow-shaped when young, deeply lobed when grown up.
zinnia-plant: Zinnias were the first flower ever grown in space — blooming aboard the ISS in 2016.
impatiance-flowers-plant: Impatiens seed pods explode when touched — scattering seeds metres away, hence one name: 'touch-me-not'.
sevanti-crysanthimum: Chrysanthemums are among NASA's top air-purifying plants — and a symbol of autumn across Asia.
spathiphylum-peace-lily: Peace lilies tell you when they're thirsty — the whole plant droops, then springs back within hours of watering.
